memory_candidates.content: When a full verify-deploy.sh/run-all.sh gate run is too expensive to run twice (pre- and post-deploy) under concurrent orchestration load, check whether orchestrate-batch-gate.sh (or the orchestrator dispatching this phase) already performed the same capture/confirm/attribute pass for this same cycle before duplicating it. deploy-baseline-lib.sh's deploy_findings_snapshot/deploy_baseline_new_findings/deploy_baseline_confirm_new_findings/deploy_baseline_unattributable_findings/deploy_baseline_self_attributable_findings functions let a single post-deploy capture be compared against a cited prior baseline instead of requiring a fresh pre-deploy capture every time.

A clean-working-tree precondition on a redeploy phase in this orchestrator is structurally unsatisfiable: deploy-headless.sh never reads git status, and the orchestrator's own EXCURSION DROPPED containment predicate manufactures uncommitted dirt every cycle by design. The correct gate for a whole-tree-regeneration phase is a measurement-integrity baseline-delta check (deploy-baseline-lib.sh), not tree cleanliness -- a future phase reaching for 'wait for a clean tree' should reconsider before self-blocking.

This harness auto-backgrounds a foreground Bash call once it runs past roughly 120-180s, even when the Bash tool's own timeout parameter is explicitly raised to 600000. The reliable workaround for a local long-running command is self-backgrounding: launch it with `nohup cmd > logfile 2>&1 & pid=$!`, record the pid, then poll liveness in repeated single-tool-call chunks of ~100s each (`while kill -0 "$pid"; do sleep 5; ...; done`) until the pid dies, then read the logfile directly -- never rely on the harness's own auto-backgrounding/notification path to resolve a long wait.
